title: Number of Steps to Reduce a Number in Binary Representation to One
summary: For a binary string representing an integer, count the steps needed to reduce it to 1 by either halving it when even or incrementing it by one when odd, ensuring it eventually reaches one.
statement: For a binary string representing an integer, count the steps needed to reduce it to 1 by either halving it when even or incrementing it by one when odd, ensuring it eventually reaches one.
constraints: s is a positive binary integer with no leading zeroes.
When even divide by two; when odd add one, repeating until one.
reference_solution:
def binary_steps_to_one(s):
 steps=carry=0
 for i in range(len(s)-1,0,-1):
  bit=int(s[i])+carry
  if bit==1:steps+=2;carry=1
  else:steps+=1
 return steps+carry

hints: Process bits right-to-left without materializing the integer.
An effective zero needs one division; an effective one needs add-one then division.
Carry remains set after adding through a one bit.
A remaining carry after non-leading bits accounts for the last operation.
editorial: A remaining carry after non-leading bits accounts for the last operation.

tests.explanation: Two divides once to reach one.
